clue.text: Down Naive, perhaps knocked back "soft drink"

parts.note: Naive read backwards is the name of a well-known French bottled brand, so the phrase describes the drink category that brand belongs to

explanation.surface: Someone innocent is knocking back what they insist is only a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naive' looks like a description of a person, but written backwards it is EVIAN, a brand of bottled spring water. The leading 'Down' is a leftover of the printed cross-reference to 13 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottled spring water is a non-alcoholic beverage, which is what a soft drink is.

clue.text: Insults involving leading actor maybe hot stuff!

indicators.note: involving means the word for insults wraps round the actor

parts.note: mud, as in slinging mud, means insults or slander
a star is a leading actor, for example

explanation.surface: Abuse hurled at a celebrity is presented as spicy gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow condiment is pungent and fiery on the tongue, a hot food.

clue.text: Approval given following change of address?

definitions.text: Approval given following change of address?

parts.words: Approval given following change of address?
parts.note: address here means speech; the cheer greets someone who has switched to saying something the listener likes, not someone who has moved house

explanation.surface: A form is approved once someone tells the office they have moved house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of address' suggests moving house, but address means a way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom of enthusiastic agreement when a speaker finally proposes something welcome.

clue.text: Almost giving in to lust for foreign currency

indicators.note: almost means the word for lustful loses its final letter

parts.note: randy means lustful or sexually eager

explanation.surface: Someone nearly succumbs to desire for an exotic banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter Y from RANDY.
explanation.definitionFit: The rand is the monetary unit of South Africa.

clue.text: Try to make a hit, and spend a lot

definitions.meaning: to strike out wildly at someone with a blow

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both swinging a punch at someone and splashing out cash extravagantly.

clue.text: Artist, interrupting every European, is a pain

indicators.note: interrupting means the artist breaks into the middle of the following words

parts.note: each means every
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter who keeps butting in on every European is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist' is the crossword's usual Royal Academician, and 'interrupting' splits the two words after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache in the ear is a kind of physical soreness; the noun phrase stands in for the ailment.

clue.text: Was non-PC, perhaps ignoring first editor

indicators.note: ignoring first means the opening letter of the bigoted word is dropped

parts.note: a sexist attitude is one example of being not politically correct

explanation.surface: An editor is accused of having been politically incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: SEXIST minus its first letter gives EXIST; add ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have existed is to have been, in the sense of being alive or real.

clue.text: Naughty daughter consumed with regret

indicators.note: the daughter is swallowed up inside the word for regret, so it encloses her

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A misbehaving girl is eaten up with remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude can mean risqué or smutty, as in a naughty joke.

clue.text: Passionate liaisons involving English diplomat's aide

parts.note: charged means emotionally intense or passionate

indicators.note: involving means the love affairs enclose the letter for English

parts.note: liaisons are love affairs

explanation.surface: Steamy romances involving an Englishman's aide at the embassy.
explanation.walkthrough: E sits inside AFFAIRS, before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: This official deputises for an ambassador, a junior envoy assisting or standing in for the head of mission.

clue.text: See 11across
Woo town's ladies, possibly after sex, at first?

definitions.text: Woo town's ladies, possibly after sex, at first?

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow that opening letter
at first means only the opening letter of the word sex is taken
possibly signals that the letters of the three words may be arranged differently

parts.note: the possessive 's is kept here as a letter S

explanation.surface: A young man courts the local women, perhaps hoping for sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange WOOTOWNSLADIES after S, the first letter of 'sex'; the whole clue describes youthful philandering.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to indulge in casual sexual adventures while young, which courting many women in hope of sex illustrates.

clue.text: Fine, after morning going crazy

indicators.note: after places the word for fine behind the word for morning

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: Things were fine until the morning, when everything went wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Running amok means behaving wildly and uncontrollably, out of control.

clue.text: Down Full description of Newcastle's surroundings?

parts.note: Newcastle upon Tyne lies in the upper right corner of England, and the adjective names that region fully with two compass points

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a complete account of the area around Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle upon Tyne is the main city of England's north-east region. The leading 'Down' is a leftover of the printed cross-reference to 8 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle sits in the region of England toward the top and to the right of the map, so its surroundings are described by that compound adjective.

clue.text: Look at some bimbo gleefully

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone stares at an empty-headed woman with obvious delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to look at someone lecherously, a leering kind of gaze.

clue.text: See 1across
Across Type of cupboard suggested by Celtic player's assistant

definitions.meaning: a kitchen sideboard with open shelves above, traditional in Wales
a theatre ... helps an actor into costume, and this one is from Wales, a Celtic nation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Celtic player' suggests a footballer for Glasgow Celtic, but it is an actor from Wales; a dresser is a backstage costume assistant. The leading 'Across' is a leftover of the printed cross-reference to 28 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: The furniture is a tall dresser in the Wales style, and a Wales-born actor's backstage helper would be called the same.

clue.text: Walked back to catch crew asleep

indicators.note: to catch means the reversed word grabs the crew inside it
back means the word for walked is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: trod is the past tense of tread, to walk
to man a ship is to crew it, so man stands for crew

explanation.surface: Someone retraced their steps to find the crew had nodded off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crew' looks like a noun, but as a verb it gives the verb to man; 'back' reverses the walking word and 'to catch' wraps it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive or sleeping, as a hibernating animal is.

clue.text: Doctor needs new china

indicators.note: new signals that the word needs is made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A doctor requires a new set of crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' looks like the country, but here it is porcelain, so it is lower case; 'new' signals the anagram of needs.
explanation.definitionFit: The German city gave its name to fine porcelain made nearby at Meissen, so the city's name denotes that porcelain.

clue.text: Not worried, he has time to pursue question surreptitiously

indicators.note: to pursue means the letter for time comes after the letter for question
worried signals that the letters of not are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A relaxed man takes his time quietly chasing up a query.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges NOT to ONT; then HE, then Q followed by T.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning secretly, on the quiet.

clue.text: Across Ring five times to describe the standard of this competition?

definitions.text: Ring five times to describe the standard of this competition?

parts.words: Ring five times to describe the standard of this competition?
parts.note: the standard is the flag, whose emblem is five interlocking rings, not a level of quality

explanation.surface: A bell is rung five times to signal how good the tournament is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' suggests quality, but it is the flag: the five-ring flag of the world's biggest sports festival. The leading 'Across' is a leftover of the printed cross-reference to 22 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: The international multi-sport festival flies a banner bearing five interlocking circles.

clue.text: One's held up by swingers at the bar

definitions.text: One's held up by swingers at the bar

parts.words: One's held up by swingers at the bar
parts.note: circus acrobats who swing grip a suspended horizontal rod, not drinkers at a pub counter

explanation.surface: Something is propped up by wife-swappers drinking at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swingers at the bar' suggests partygoers in a pub, but they are acrobats swinging from a horizontal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: The circus apparatus is a bar hung on ropes that aerialists grip and swing from.

clue.text: Western brought in such a lot of dollars

definitions.text: Western brought in such a lot of dollars

parts.words: Western brought in such a lot of dollars
parts.note: a Sergio Leone cowboy film's title says how much money it is about, a handful

explanation.surface: A cowboy film earned so much at the box office.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1964 spaghetti western starring Clint Eastwood is 'A ___ of Dollars'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a handful, the quantity named in that film's title.

clue.text: Loudly 12'd, and was laughing mockingly

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loudly
the answer to 12 across with -ed added means looked at lecherously, which is leered

explanation.surface: Someone stared loudly and also sneered.
explanation.walkthrough: '12'd' turns the 12 across word into a past-tense verb; a synonym for that is LEERED.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleer is an old verb meaning to grin or jeer derisively.

clue.text: Boy rebel may be running out of energy-I try to organise support

indicators.note: running signals rearranging the letters of boy rebel, and out of says the letter for energy is lost from them

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tired young rebel tries to rally people behind a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop E from BOYREBEL and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who campaigns to win backing from legislators is a campaigner seeking influence; the clue speaks in that campaigner's voice.

clue.text: Cowardly letting out second cry of pain? So it is

definitions.text: Cowardly letting out second cry of pain? So it is

indicators.note: letting out means the exclamation is released, removed from the word for cowardly

parts.note: yellow means cowardly
ow is a cry of pain, and the remainder is itself a cry, making this the second

explanation.surface: A coward lets out a second scream of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: YELLOW minus OW leaves YELL, which is itself a cry: 'So it is' confirms the result is another shout.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud shout or scream is what someone in pain lets out.

clue.text: See 17down
Get stuck, dictating post

indicators.note: dictating means the word is spoken out to a listener, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: to jam is to get stuck

explanation.surface: A clerk gets stuck while dictating the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is an upright side piece of a door or window frame.

clue.text: Young woman getting over a festive occasion

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting over puts the young woman above the A

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman recovers from a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a celebratory event or entertainment.

clue.text: Mushy peas served somewhere church

indicators.note: mushy means mashed up, so the letters of peas are broken and reformed

explanation.surface: Mushy peas are served up somewhere in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushy peas' looks like the British side dish of mashed marrowfat peas, but 'Mushy' rearranges PEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is a semicircular recess at the east end of a church building.

clue.text: Personal possessions characteristic of a soldier?

definitions.meaning: the belongings of a private, the lowest army rank

explanation.definitionFit: The legal term means individually owned assets, and read literally it is what belongs to a private in the army.

clue.text: Dance around in church, showing common origins

indicators.note: in means the reversed dance sits inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: around means the dance is turned back to front

parts.note: the tango is a dance

explanation.surface: People circle while dancing in church, revealing shared roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals reversing the dance, and 'in' puts it inside the Church of England abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognate words or peoples are related by descent from a shared ancestor.
